text:
GRU theory links update gates to slow memory modes and reset gates to state-Jacobian dynamics; gate saturation alone does not establish harmful forgetting. Foundational work predates 2023: [Gating creates slow modes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00025), [Fast Saturating Gate](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.01348). Suggested single-network probes: update/reset gate distributions and saturation fractions on nonpadding steps; hidden-state changes; lag-dependent Jacobian-vector products measuring perturbation survival. Separate retained state sensitivity from target-score sensitivity: remembered information may contribute little to candidate discrimination. These are diagnostic adaptations, not established GRU4Rec accuracy predictors.

Recent gradient-conflict research examines competing updates within shared parameters ([2024 study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18615)). Adaptation: compute gradient norms, cosine similarities and negative-dot-product rates across training-user groups or sequence positions, separately for embeddings, recurrent gates and output parameters. Validate interference with a small temporary update and measure its effect on another group's loss, then restore parameters. Negative cosine indicates local opposition; it does not by itself demonstrate harmful generalization.

Intervention checks provide stronger component attribution than gradients alone. [Activation-patching guidance (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255) emphasizes corruption choice and metric dependence; [AtP* (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00745) documents gradient-approximation false negatives. For one trained GRU, patch gate/state activations between matched original and perturbed histories; measure positive–negative score margins and ranking changes. Compare targeted patches with random components, matched perturbation magnitudes, sham patches and parameter-randomization controls. Verify selected gradient estimates with exact interventions. Preserve left-padding and final-nonpadding readout; use validation HR@10 to assess proposed improvements without assuming stronger recency helps.
